chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, who said: I heard Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام say:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام used to say, concerning a man who inserts his hand into his nose and blood reaches his five fingers: He said, “He should clean it, and he does not repeat the wudu (ablution).”

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abā al-Ḥasan, the Imam عليه السلام transmitting the report
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, whose ruling is being quoted
key_terms.الدَّمُ: blood that came out and touched the fingers
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُنَقِّيهِ: he should cleanse or remove it

ai.seo_question: Does nosebleed or blood on the hand invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding blood that comes from the nose onto the hand. It states that the blood should be cleaned, but it does not invalidate the wudu (ablution), so repeating the wudu is not required.
